newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore visit deepened ties, Albright says.
newsitem.headline: Singapore visit deepened ties, Albright says.

text.p: U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright's visit to Singapore has strengthened bilateral ties, Albright and a Singapore Foreign Ministry spokesman said on Tuesday.
"I think that our relations are good and on a very solid foundation," Albright told reporters after talks with Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong.
"They understand and appreciate the U.S. role in the region and we have close ties, economically, politically and strategically," she said.
But Albright said she had raised human rights issues with Singapore, which practises censorship and imposes restrictions on the media in various areas to protect what it views as basic values.
"I did raise some human rights issues, especially the freedom of the press, with the prime minister," she said without elaborating.

The visit "deepened the strong bilateral ties enjoyed by the two countries. It has also reinforced the close cooperation on economic, political and security issues," Singapore's Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MFA) said in a statement.
Albright arrived in Singapore on Tuesday morning and had individual meetings in the afternoon with Goh, Senior Minister Lee Kuan Yew, and Foreign Minister Shanmugam Jayakumar.
The brief MFA statement said Albright discussed a wide range of international issues with Goh and Lee and they agreed both countries should continue to cooperate closely.
Albright and Jayakumar reviewed the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) Regional Forum and post-ministerial meetings they both attended in Malaysia before Albright's Singapore visit.
They "expressed satisfaction at the outcome of these meetings," the MFA statement said.

Earlier Albright toured a manufacturing plant of a U.S. company with 19,000 employees in Singapore, and called the operation: "a perfect example of the future of how globalisation serves the purposes of manufacturing and jobs in many countries at the same time."
"As long as I'm Secretary of State we're going to be working towards the free trade area that we hope to have by the year 2020," Albright said.
The Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation forum, which includes Singapore and the United States among its 18 members, has set a goal of free trade by 2020.
Economic and defence ties between the United States and Singapore are extensive. Singapore provides logistic support and repair facilities for U.S. naval forces in the region.
But ties have been ruffled by disagreements over the past few years.

The issues have ranged from the caning of American teenager Michael Fay, which triggered a furore in the United States, to differences on how to treat the ruling military council in Burma or Washington's relations with China.
Albright leaves Singapore on Wednesday to return to the United States.
